reasons.C: Closest movement and stance: blunt assertive declaratives, semicolon-linked parallel clauses ('they have not read...; they have not read...'), double dashes, first-person asides and a rhetorical question, in the period register of the passage; the repeated sympathy for teachers lays it on a little thick.
reasons.B: Right period feel (double dashes, 'any one', semicolons, rhetorical question), but the mannered wit ('I fancy', 'wears a cap and gown', 'melancholy') is more ironic than the passage's flat severity, and the contraction 'we've' breaks its register.
reasons.A: Modern, measured and impersonal: even mid-length sentences, no dashes, no first-person intrusion, no rhetorical questions, and a balanced hedging tone unlike the passage's sweeping, combative assertions.
